content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_8fb667cfb8d1e8dcc7a182\", \"title\": \"Combo Fighter GDD\", \"revisionId\": \"8fb667cfb8\", \"text\": \"Overview\\n1. Game Overview\\nTitle: Combo Fighter\\nGenre: Merge puzzle auto battler\\nPlatform: (iOS / Android)\\nCore Loop Summary:\\nPlace fight-action tetris shaped pieces on a game board and watch the character fight hordes of enemies.\\n2. Core Gameplay\\nPlayer Actions:\\nDrag tetris shaped pieces onto the game board, merge pieces to upgrade them, connect the pieces to create combos to deal extra damage, fill the board with more pieces to deal more attacks and/or damage.\\nDraw additional pieces randomly to place them on the board. Optimize your spaces and combo connections.\\nGain experience by defeating monsters and merging tiles. Experience levels up the hero and the player can choose a skill upgrade.\\nWhen the game ends, the player can upgrade the hero's Max HP, HP regen rate during the game, and attack power.\\nGame Objective:\\nDefeat all the waves of monsters in each level.\\nFailure Condition:\\nThe player\\u2019s HP reaches 0 from monster attacks.\\n3. Game Flow\\nHome Screen: Start button, current level displayed, three upgrade buttons.\\nGameplay: 4 to 5 minutes per level. The game switches from preparation phase to battle phase with occasional pop up dialogue for roguelite skill upgrades.\\nResult Screen: Displays rewards earned. Gold only in MVP.\\nUpgrades: Hero\\u2019s Max HP, HP regen rate, hero\\u2019s attack power bonus\\n4. Level Design\\n35 hand crafted levels in MVP\\nMonsters will have increased HP and attack damage as level progresses.\\nLevels will have obstacles on the board to create difficulty. These obstacles can be removed with silver earned in the level. These obstacles reset each game.\\nLevels will have different starting points for first combo piece placement. Each level will also have a set of possible pieces that can be dropped and their drop rate.\\n5. Art & Visual Style\\nThe top portion of the screen is dedicated to combat visualization during battle phase, the bottom portion only displays the puzzle board.\\nDuring intermission between waves of monsters, the camera shifts down to reveal a puzzle board + three slots staging area for players to obtain new puzzle pieces, this is the preparation phase. Pressing a FIGHT button will shift the camera back up and transition into the battle phase.\\nCharacter Designs: Simple Chibi style 3D characters.\\nUI: Simple standard UI, home screen with minimal buttons.\\n6. Audio\\nMusic: None\\nSFX: Standard fighting sounds.\\n7. Monetization\\nAds: None in MVP\\n8. Ugly Game Mockups\\nHome Screen with 3 upgrade choices, start button, coin balance and settings button\\nGameplay\\nGame Starts, 3 pieces randomly selected for players to choose from.\\nPlayers drag pieces onto the board, the character starts doing loop animation of the attacks on the board.\\nThe values showing total punch, kick and special attack power changes real time based on pieces on the board\\nThe dmg/s calculation also updates real time as pieces are being placed\\nThe Info button will bring up a pop up of available moves (see below)\\nPressing refresh will consume gold if available, and refreshes the 3 cards.\\nHolding a tile under the finger will change the refresh button to SELL. If a player moves pieces over the sell button, the piece will be sold.\\nCoin balance and health is displayed near the top\\nAfter pressing the fight button, the camera shifts upward to increase the size of the fight scene and the battle starts. This phase requires no input action from the players\\nInfo Pop Up\\nSimple End Game Screen\\nDOCUMENT DOES NOT END HERE! MAKE SURE TO CLICK ON THE OTHER TABS (\\u201cDetailed Mechanics\\u201d) IN THIS DOCUMENT ON THE LEFT SIDE BAR IN GOOGLE DOCS\\nDetailed Mechanics\\n1. Starting A Level\\nLevel starts with a 6x6 empty game board.\\nThe level designer will indicate which left most square tile will be the first tile that starts the combo, if tiles are not placed here, There are no combos and only Singular attacks.\\nPlayers are presented with a staging area with 3 random tiles at start. They can use these tiles on their board or sell them, or they can press the refresh button which costs silver to be dealt three more random tiles. Pressing the fight buttons begins the battle phase. The tiles themselves are free, only refresh costs money.\\nTiles that remain on the board when the refresh button is pressed are sold automatically for 10 gold each.\\nOnce the battle phase starts, the character automatically executes the fighting sequence based on the tiles placed. The enemies will approach from the right side of the screen. If combos are not present on the board, then the player will perform one attack each of punch and/or kicks and/or special attacks if those action tiles exist. There is a 0.6 seconds delay between these attack animations, and these tiles that are not part of the combo will have an attack power penalty. So for example if a combo does not exist, but There are P K and S tiles on the board, the player will do Punch (basic jab animation) \\u2192 0.6 second delay \\u2192 Kick (basic roundhouse kick animation) \\u2192 0.6 second delay \\u2192 Special attack (fireball) \\u2192 0.6 second delay \\u2192 repeat\\nWhen the monster crosses the green line seen below, the character will automatically execute the fighting combo. When the monster crosses the red line, they will start to attack the player.\\nIf There are no monsters within melee range of the player, the player will execute a ranged attack based on the total special attack power, with a 0.8 seconds delay between each attack. (Fireball Hadouken animation)\\nFireball will hit 3 enemies before disappearing. This can be upgraded. So in this case we can upgrade a fireball to hit the left most 6 enemies.\\nPlayers will gain experience and silver from killing monsters. Experience will allow the player to level up within the game and select some random upgrades. Silver is used to obtain more tiles during the preparation phase.\\nWhen the wave of monsters is defeated, the camera shifts back down exposing the staging area and we are back to the preparation phase where players get to acquire more tiles and optimize their placements on the board. The game ends in a loss if the player is defeated and HP reaches 0.\\nThe game ends in victory if the player defeats all waves of monsters.\\nPLEASE NOTE THAT THE AMOUNT OF SILVER AND EXP RECEIVED IS NOT BASED ON MONSTER TYPE KILLED OR QUANTITY OF MONSTERS KILLED. Instead, we are introducing a system that allows designers to set the amount of exp and silver a player will receive each wave, and we divide that across the monsters in that wave..\\nBlock Merging & Rearrangement\\nWhen the preparation phase starts, There will be 3 blocks spawned in the bottom area to place or merge.\\nHolding a piece will show possible placements with highlighted corners.\\nWhen the tiles have mergeable counterparts in the board, the mergeable tile on the board will have a glowing outline.\\nLike the video below.\\nScreenRecording_11-11-2025 16-11-07_1.MP4\\nWhile arranging the placement of blocks, players can move board tiles to the bottom area and rearrange them back and forth.\\nThe only limitation is that 3 blocks can be stored on the bottom part.\\nOnce players decide to continue fighting, clicking the \\u201cFight\\u201d button, the pieces left on the bottom would be sold automatically.\\nPlayers can merge the blocks in the bottom part.\\n2. Combat Power and Damage Calculation\\nThere are three types of action tiles: Punch (P), Kick (K) and Special Attack (S). The corresponding tile colors are green, blue, and red.\\nTiles will display the full combat power they provide. Not penalized discounted power.\\nTiles will come in different shapes\\nPunch has a base attack power of 10, Kick is 20, and Special Attack is 40\\nThe same tiles can be merged and upgraded to increase their power. Tiles that are not part of a combo and only contribute half power are called \\u201cAssist Tiles,\\u201d they are dimmed visually. When merged it simply sums the combat power. So level 1 Punch = 10, level 2 punch = 20, level 3 punch = 40 (Requires 2x level 2) They do not need to be connected to any pieces to contribute. They just need to be on the board.\\nThe individual power of the combo is shown in the UI like seen here below.\\nThe damage per attack sequence is based on the only combo on the board, each board can only have a max of one combo, and for each action in the combo, the damage dealt is calculated using the following:\\n[Action Power] = [Tile Power + (50%*(SUM of assist tile power))] * Combo Bonus Multiplier\\nThis calculates the individual action power for the combo\\nCombo multipliers are pre-assigned by game designers. Here is an example of a combo calculation.\\nSmall sample list of combos and their multiplier and base DPS, this is accessed via the info button during the game. The character at the top animates the combo punching air/dummy when the player selects a combo.\\n3. Combo Creation UI/UX\\n4. Game Currencies and Homescreen Upgrades\\nThere will be 3 different upgradeable stats at the home screen which are persistent across sessions and levels. The currency used to upgrade is gold. We can consider adding an ad watch when players run out of gold.\\nThey will be extended with gears or other upgrades that we can use later on. So for the implementation, please be aware that we can extend upgrades.\\nAttack Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) So 100% + 2% + 2% + 2% + 2% (Level 4 = 108% * attack)\\nHealth Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) Same as attack. So level 5 health increase = 110% * base HP of 100 = 110 total Hp\\nHealth Regen Increase (+0.02% per second, Additive) So level 7 is 2% base regen + (0.02% * 7 = 0.14%) final health regen = 2.14% HP regen per second.\\n5. Monsters, Stats, Damage Assignment, Stagger and Loot\\nEach monster when hit is \\u201cstunned\\u201d for 0.25 seconds. However this has a cooldown of 1.5 seconds. This means after being stunned, the earliest the next time the same monster can be stunned again is 1.25 seconds later because 1.5 second cooldown from first stun - 0.25 stun duration = 1.25 seconds after end of first stun.\\nMonster attack animation should be from start to finish should be 1 second, with damage dealt at 0.8 second timestamp\\nWe do not need more than 5 monsters for MVP\\nWhen monsters are hit, we display damage dealt using standard RPG text VFX. We then display the monster health bar permanently above their head, but we do not display numerical values for their HP\\nMonster speed is the second it takes to move from edge of screen to crossing the monster attack line. Attack speed is expressed in seconds per attack.\\n| Monster Name | Base HP | Damage | Seconds Per Attack | Move Speed |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| [USERNAME_37755] | 10 | 10 | 1 | 10 |\\n| [USERNAME_53102] | 10 | 10 | 1 | 10 |\\n| [USERNAME_53103] | 10 | 10 | 1 | 10 |\\n| [USERNAME_53104] | 10 | 10 | 1 | 10 |\\n| [USERNAME_53105] | 10 | 10 | 1 | 10 |\\n6. Levels\\nWe need to let designers designate starting positions for each level.\\nEach level will also have obstacles that need to be removed via silver.\\nEach level will have 15 waves of monsters\\nEach wave of monsters will get an HP and damage multiplier bonus following a standard algorithm\\nHP multiplier for monster is wave # * XXX\\nDamage multiplier for monster is wave # * YYY\\nWe need to utilize the monster spawning system from Zombie Match, this will allow designers to specify monsters spawn timing and quantity\\nLevel Design Tools\\nEach level will have monsters, monsters spawn, their stats, board type, and the pool of tiles available.\\nSo what\\u2019s needed from a level is that\\nLEVEL NAME\\nMonster Track\\nWaves\\nMonster type,\\nMonster amount,\\nSpawn Duration (fixed or interval)\\n[USERNAME_5859]\\u2019s stats (dmg & HP)\\nWave multiplier for damage & HP (separate)\\nAnother wave\\nMonster type,\\nMonster amount,\\nSpawn Duration (fixed or interval)\\n[USERNAME_5859]\\u2019s stats (dmg & HP)\\nWave multiplier for damage & HP (separate)\\nBoard Info\\nPool of tiles\\nAbility to select available tiles used in that level\\nSpawn rate of individual tiles\\nSpawn rate of colors (?)\\nSpawn rate of shapes (?)\\nPool types (if necessary later on)\\nStart and exit nodes  (if necessary later on)\\n7. Player Starting Stats\\nBase player HP is 100\\nBase player regen rate is 2% per second, but this is only during the \\u201cfight\\u201d phase and not the prep phase.\\nBase attack is 0, no tiles placed = no damage.\\n8. Experience Table and Skill Choices\\nFor XP tables Combo Fighter Design Details\\nFor Silver Tables Combo Fighter Design Details\\nXP and Silver.png\\nExperience points will reset after each attempt, meaning that it will start from the scratch in every level attempt.\\nExperience will be gained from the actions below,\\nMerging blocks yield less XP\\nKilling enemies yields more XP\\nRoguelite skills don't require any currency to use. Just selecting the desired one out of all 3 options.\\nThe skills will have 3 phases that can be improved further after selecting the first phase.\\nRoguelite Skills In MVP\\nIncrease Punch Damage by 35%   (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) But for this one I think keeping it at +35% regardless of level is a better start.\\nIncrease Kick Damage by 20%   (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) But for this one I think keeping it at +20% regardless of level is a better start.\\nIncrease Special Attack Damage by 15%   (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) But for this one I think keeping it at +15% regardless of level is a better start.\\nIncrease All Damage by 10%  (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) I think this one should scale.\\nLevel 1 +10%\\nLevel 2 +15%\\nLevel 3 +20%\\nLevel 4 +25%\\nLevel 5 +30%\\nIncrease Max HP by 50% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) But for this one I think keeping it at +50% regardless of level is a better start.\\nReduce Attack Cooldown by 20% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) But I think max 2 levels is enough for this:\\nLevel 1 Reduce Attack Cooldown by 20%\\nLevel 2 Reduce Attack Cooldown by 30%\\nThis means by level 2, the player will have 20% + 30% cooldown. The pause between combos will be half as long.\\nRestore 100% HP (No levels, but can be repeatedly chosen, if it appears)\\nIncrease HP Regen by 1% / sec (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nRestore +1 HP Per Enemy Hit (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nGain 60 Silver (I think when this skill appears, it should have the rewarded amount = the last wave player has finished rewarded amount)\\nGain X Gold (Can only be obtained ONCE per run, This should always be 50% of the level reward)\\nLevel Up a Random Tile (Can be repeatedly chosen)\\nSlow Enemies Move Speed by 15% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nGet 1 Free Refresh\\nIncrease Tile Merging Exp by 25% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nIncrease Monster Exp by 25% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nIncrease All XP gained by 10% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nIncrease Assist Tile Power by 20% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nDamage Immunity for 5 seconds (Deprecated)\\nGet a Level 2 Small Square P/K/S Tile (3 variants to this, tile will appear automatically on board, if board is full it appears in staging slots, if slots also full, it will appear in the very next refresh) SKIP FOR ALPHA\\nFireball Can Hit 3 Additional Enemies (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nCombos with 4 Hits or Less Gains 15% Bonus Damage (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nCombos with 5+ Hits Gains 20% Bonus Damage (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\n9. Combo List and their Bonus Multipliers\\nHere\\n10. VFX and animations\\nCombo tile VFX when character is attacking.\\n11. Mechanics Spreadsheet link: HERE\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_8fb667cfb8d1e8dcc7a182", "title": "Combo Fighter GDD", "revisionId": "8fb667cfb8", "text": "Overview
1. Game Overview
Title: Combo Fighter
Genre: Merge puzzle auto battler
Platform: (iOS / Android)
Core Loop Summary:
Place fight-action tetris shaped pieces on a game board and watch the character fight hordes of enemies.
2. Core Gameplay
Player Actions:
Drag tetris shaped pieces onto the game board, merge pieces to upgrade them, connect the pieces to create combos to deal extra damage, fill the board with more pieces to deal more attacks and/or damage.
Draw additional pieces randomly to place them on the board. Optimize your spaces and combo connections.
Gain experience by defeating monsters and merging tiles. Experience levels up the hero and the player can choose a skill upgrade.
When the game ends, the player can upgrade the hero's Max HP, HP regen rate during the game, and attack power.
Game Objective:
Defeat all the waves of monsters in each level.
Failure Condition:
The player’s HP reaches 0 from monster attacks.
3. Game Flow
Home Screen: Start button, current level displayed, three upgrade buttons.
Gameplay: 4 to 5 minutes per level. The game switches from preparation phase to battle phase with occasional pop up dialogue for roguelite skill upgrades.
Result Screen: Displays rewards earned. Gold only in MVP.
Upgrades: Hero’s Max HP, HP regen rate, hero’s attack power bonus
4. Level Design
35 hand crafted levels in MVP
Monsters will have increased HP and attack damage as level progresses.
Levels will have obstacles on the board to create difficulty. These obstacles can be removed with silver earned in the level. These obstacles reset each game.
Levels will have different starting points for first combo piece placement. Each level will also have a set of possible pieces that can be dropped and their drop rate.
5. Art & Visual Style
The top portion of the screen is dedicated to combat visualization during battle phase, the bottom portion only displays the puzzle board.
During intermission between waves of monsters, the camera shifts down to reveal a puzzle board + three slots staging area for players to obtain new puzzle pieces, this is the preparation phase. Pressing a FIGHT button will shift the camera back up and transition into the battle phase.
Character Designs: Simple Chibi style 3D characters.
UI: Simple standard UI, home screen with minimal buttons.
6. Audio
Music: None
SFX: Standard fighting sounds.
7. Monetization
Ads: None in MVP
8. Ugly Game Mockups
Home Screen with 3 upgrade choices, start button, coin balance and settings button
Gameplay
Game Starts, 3 pieces randomly selected for players to choose from.
Players drag pieces onto the board, the character starts doing loop animation of the attacks on the board.
The values showing total punch, kick and special attack power changes real time based on pieces on the board
The dmg/s calculation also updates real time as pieces are being placed
The Info button will bring up a pop up of available moves (see below)
Pressing refresh will consume gold if available, and refreshes the 3 cards.
Holding a tile under the finger will change the refresh button to SELL. If a player moves pieces over the sell button, the piece will be sold.
Coin balance and health is displayed near the top
After pressing the fight button, the camera shifts upward to increase the size of the fight scene and the battle starts. This phase requires no input action from the players
Info Pop Up
Simple End Game Screen
DOCUMENT DOES NOT END HERE! MAKE SURE TO CLICK ON THE OTHER TABS (“Detailed Mechanics”) IN THIS DOCUMENT ON THE LEFT SIDE BAR IN GOOGLE DOCS
Detailed Mechanics
1. Starting A Level
Level starts with a 6x6 empty game board.
The level designer will indicate which left most square tile will be the first tile that starts the combo, if tiles are not placed here, There are no combos and only Singular attacks.
Players are presented with a staging area with 3 random tiles at start. They can use these tiles on their board or sell them, or they can press the refresh button which costs silver to be dealt three more random tiles. Pressing the fight buttons begins the battle phase. The tiles themselves are free, only refresh costs money.
Tiles that remain on the board when the refresh button is pressed are sold automatically for 10 gold each.
Once the battle phase starts, the character automatically executes the fighting sequence based on the tiles placed. The enemies will approach from the right side of the screen. If combos are not present on the board, then the player will perform one attack each of punch and/or kicks and/or special attacks if those action tiles exist. There is a 0.6 seconds delay between these attack animations, and these tiles that are not part of the combo will have an attack power penalty. So for example if a combo does not exist, but There are P K and S tiles on the board, the player will do Punch (basic jab animation) → 0.6 second delay → Kick (basic roundhouse kick animation) → 0.6 second delay → Special attack (fireball) → 0.6 second delay → repeat
When the monster crosses the green line seen below, the character will automatically execute the fighting combo. When the monster crosses the red line, they will start to attack the player.
If There are no monsters within melee range of the player, the player will execute a ranged attack based on the total special attack power, with a 0.8 seconds delay between each attack. (Fireball Hadouken animation)
Fireball will hit 3 enemies before disappearing. This can be upgraded. So in this case we can upgrade a fireball to hit the left most 6 enemies.
Players will gain experience and silver from killing monsters. Experience will allow the player to level up within the game and select some random upgrades. Silver is used to obtain more tiles during the preparation phase.
When the wave of monsters is defeated, the camera shifts back down exposing the staging area and we are back to the preparation phase where players get to acquire more tiles and optimize their placements on the board. The game ends in a loss if the player is defeated and HP reaches 0.
The game ends in victory if the player defeats all waves of monsters.
PLEASE NOTE THAT THE AMOUNT OF SILVER AND EXP RECEIVED IS NOT BASED ON MONSTER TYPE KILLED OR QUANTITY OF MONSTERS KILLED. Instead, we are introducing a system that allows designers to set the amount of exp and silver a player will receive each wave, and we divide that across the monsters in that wave..
Block Merging & Rearrangement
When the preparation phase starts, There will be 3 blocks spawned in the bottom area to place or merge.
Holding a piece will show possible placements with highlighted corners.
When the tiles have mergeable counterparts in the board, the mergeable tile on the board will have a glowing outline.
Like the video below.
ScreenRecording_11-11-2025 16-11-07_1.MP4
While arranging the placement of blocks, players can move board tiles to the bottom area and rearrange them back and forth.
The only limitation is that 3 blocks can be stored on the bottom part.
Once players decide to continue fighting, clicking the “Fight” button, the pieces left on the bottom would be sold automatically.
Players can merge the blocks in the bottom part.
2. Combat Power and Damage Calculation
There are three types of action tiles: Punch (P), Kick (K) and Special Attack (S). The corresponding tile colors are green, blue, and red.
Tiles will display the full combat power they provide. Not penalized discounted power.
Tiles will come in different shapes
Punch has a base attack power of 10, Kick is 20, and Special Attack is 40
The same tiles can be merged and upgraded to increase their power. Tiles that are not part of a combo and only contribute half power are called “Assist Tiles,” they are dimmed visually. When merged it simply sums the combat power. So level 1 Punch = 10, level 2 punch = 20, level 3 punch = 40 (Requires 2x level 2) They do not need to be connected to any pieces to contribute. They just need to be on the board.
The individual power of the combo is shown in the UI like seen here below.
The damage per attack sequence is based on the only combo on the board, each board can only have a max of one combo, and for each action in the combo, the damage dealt is calculated using the following:
[Action Power] = [Tile Power + (50%*(SUM of assist tile power))] * Combo Bonus Multiplier
This calculates the individual action power for the combo
Combo multipliers are pre-assigned by game designers. Here is an example of a combo calculation.
Small sample list of combos and their multiplier and base DPS, this is accessed via the info button during the game. The character at the top animates the combo punching air/dummy when the player selects a combo.
3. Combo Creation UI/UX
4. Game Currencies and Homescreen Upgrades
There will be 3 different upgradeable stats at the home screen which are persistent across sessions and levels. The currency used to upgrade is gold. We can consider adding an ad watch when players run out of gold.
They will be extended with gears or other upgrades that we can use later on. So for the implementation, please be aware that we can extend upgrades.
Attack Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) So 100% + 2% + 2% + 2% + 2% (Level 4 = 108% * attack)
Health Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) Same as attack. So level 5 health increase = 110% * base HP of 100 = 110 total Hp
Health Regen Increase (+0.02% per second, Additive) So level 7 is 2% base regen + (0.02% * 7 = 0.14%) final health regen = 2.14% HP regen per second.
5. Monsters, Stats, Damage Assignment, Stagger and Loot
Each monster when hit is “stunned” for 0.25 seconds. However this has a cooldown of 1.5 seconds. This means after being stunned, the earliest the next time the same monster can be stunned again is 1.25 seconds later because 1.5 second cooldown from first stun - 0.25 stun duration = 1.25 seconds after end of first stun.
Monster attack animation should be from start to finish should be 1 second, with damage dealt at 0.8 second timestamp
We do not need more than 5 monsters for MVP
When monsters are hit, we display damage dealt using standard RPG text VFX. We then display the monster health bar permanently above their head, but we do not display numerical values for their HP
Monster speed is the second it takes to move from edge of screen to crossing the monster attack line. Attack speed is expressed in seconds per attack.

6. Levels
We need to let designers designate starting positions for each level.
Each level will also have obstacles that need to be removed via silver.
Each level will have 15 waves of monsters
Each wave of monsters will get an HP and damage multiplier bonus following a standard algorithm
HP multiplier for monster is wave # * XXX
Damage multiplier for monster is wave # * YYY
We need to utilize the monster spawning system from Zombie Match, this will allow designers to specify monsters spawn timing and quantity
Level Design Tools
Each level will have monsters, monsters spawn, their stats, board type, and the pool of tiles available.
So what’s needed from a level is that

7. Player Starting Stats

Base player regen rate is 2% per second, but this is only during the “fight” phase and not the prep phase.
Base attack is 0, no tiles placed = no damage.
8. Experience Table and Skill Choices

{"result":"[{\"id\": \"page_combo_gdd\", \"space_id\": \"space_PROD\", \"parent_id\": \"page_prod_home\", \"title\": \"Combo Fighter \\u2014 Game Design Document\", \"body\": \"

Combo Fighter is a merge / auto-battler prototype: the player drags Tetris-shaped pieces onto a board, merges matching pieces to upgrade them, connects them into combos, and then watches an auto-battle phase resolve the round. It was the last new concept Harmony Games took to a testable build \\u2014 a skeleton crew put a playable MVP together in roughly four to five weeks (late 2025 into January 2026). Of the three prototypes we shipped to store test tracks it posted the strongest early engagement, but it remains parked: we haven't put UA spend behind it yet to see whether that engagement holds at scale.

Core Mechanics

A round has two distinct phases. The build phase is board manipulation; the battle phase is hands-off resolution.

Build phase

  • Drag & place. The tray offers Tetris-shaped pieces (I, L, S, T, square). The player drags a piece onto the board; it snaps to the grid.
  • Merge to upgrade. Two same-tier pieces of the same type that touch merge into the next tier \\u2014 the familiar merge-2 loop, but on shaped pieces rather than single cells.
  • Connect for combos. Pieces wired into a contiguous chain form a combo; longer chains grant a battle-phase multiplier, so board layout drives power.

Battle phase

  • The assembled board becomes the player's squad and auto-battles the level's wave. No input during battle \\u2014 the round is won or lost on how the board was built.
  • Rewards are gold only. Gold funds re-rolls and starting-piece upgrades. No gems, no energy, no second currency in the MVP.

Ads: None in MVP. There is no ad SDK, no interstitials, and no rewarded placements in the prototype. Monetization was deliberately deferred until the core loop proved it retained \\u2014 the test builds measured engagement and retention only.

Art direction

Simple Chibi-style 3D characters on a clean board. The look was chosen to be cheap to produce at prototype scale while still reading as a finished game in a store screenshot.

Scope \\u2014 MVP

The build track was a 35-level MVP carved out of a 163-level full design. The MVP existed to answer one question \\u2014 does the merge-plus-auto-battle loop hold a player past the first session \\u2014 before committing to the remaining content and the deeper progression curve.

  • Shipped in MVP: 35 levels, drag/merge/connect build loop, auto-battle resolution, gold economy, Chibi 3D art.
  • Designed but not built: levels 36\\u2013163, meta-progression between runs, monetization surface, live-ops events.

Builds & Early Retention

Three test builds went out over roughly two weeks in January and early February 2026. D1 retention climbed with each build even as install volume swung with test-track promotion.

BuildRelease dateInstallsD1 retention
1.0.62Jan 21, 202612725%
1.0.72Jan 25, 202624431%
1.0.88Feb 4, 20263043%

Session length was the standout signal: Combo Fighter averaged roughly 60 minutes of play on the day of install (D0) \\u2014 the best of the three games we prototyped. By 1.0.88 the loop was tightening and D1 had reached 43% on a small install base, but we have not yet validated that at scale on a larger install base.

Related Pages

Prototype targets and the retention bar this work was measured against live in the H1 product objectives: Product OKRs \\u2014 2025 H1.

This page documents how gameplay telemetry flows from the Unity client into our analytics warehouse. It is the reference for anyone instrumenting a new event or writing a Snowflake query for a dashboard. For where this sits in the broader system, see Architecture Overview.

Scope: hybrid-casual titles across the studio \\u2014 Domino Delights (codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" on store), and Combo Fighter. All three share one instrumentation library and one pipeline.

Pipeline overview

The Unity client emits events through the Firebase Analytics SDK. From there a game-analytics pipeline streams events into AWS, transforms them, and lands them in object storage, from which the warehouse loads. The stages:

  • Unity client \\u2192 Firebase \\u2014 the client batches events and hands them to the Firebase Analytics SDK on-device.
  • Firebase \\u2192 Kinesis \\u2014 events are forwarded into an AWS Kinesis stream for ingestion.
  • Kinesis \\u2192 Glue \\u2014 an AWS Glue job validates and transforms records (flattens the event envelope, casts types, partitions by date).
  • Glue \\u2192 S3 \\u2014 both a raw/ and a processed/ prefix are written to S3.
  • S3 \\u2192 Snowflake \\u2014 the BI/warehouse layer loads from the S3 processed/ prefix. Analysts query Snowflake for dashboards and ad-hoc analysis.

Install attribution is handled separately by Singular (our MMP); attribution results are joined into Snowflake for UA reporting rather than flowing through the client event stream.

Event categories

Every event carries a common envelope (app version, platform, device class, session id, server timestamp). At a high level events fall into five categories:

CategoryFires onUsed for
SessionApp open / close, foreground / backgroundDAU, session length, retention curves
ProgressionLevel start / complete / failDifficulty tuning, funnel drop-off
Resource / economyCurrency and life grant / spendSink-source balance, economy health
Ad impressionRewarded / interstitial shown & completedAd revenue, fill rate, eCPM
Client errorHandled exceptions, load stallsCrash triage, release health

Load macro (Glue \\u2192 S3 \\u2192 Snowflake)

The warehouse pulls the Glue output from S3 with a scheduled COPY. Sketch of the load:

sql

The COPY is append-only and idempotent per partition \\u2014 never TRUNCATE the landing table to \\\"reload\\\", or you drop history the marts depend on. Backfills replay a specific dt= partition only.

Adding or changing an event

  • Register the event name and payload in the shared instrumentation library before shipping \\u2014 do not free-type event names in game code.
  • New fields must be nullable; the Glue transform tolerates extra keys but will not backfill missing ones.
  • Flag any type change (int \\u2192 string, etc.) to eng before release \\u2014 it breaks the Snowflake COPY column mapping.
\", \"body_format\": \"storage\", \"status\": \"current\", \"version\": 6, \"author_id\": \"user_EMPLOYEE_0031\", \"created_at\": \"2024-02-01T17:06:15Z\", \"updated_at\": \"2025-11-01T11:06:51Z\"}, {\"id\": \"page_arch_overview\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_eng_home\", \"title\": \"Architecture Overview\", \"body\": \"

This page describes the runtime architecture behind Harmony Games' live mobile titles — Domino Delights (internal codename Game of Dominoes / GoD) and Zombie Match 3D (store name Puzzles vs Zombies) — plus the shared platform that Combo Fighter and future titles ride on. It is the canonical starting point for new engineers; deep-dives live on the linked pages.

All of this runs in a single AWS account per environment (staging and prod). Infra is defined in AWS CDK (v2, TypeScript) — there is no click-ops. If it's not in the CDK app, it doesn't exist. See the AWS Infrastructure Guide for the account layout and deploy flow.

Client tier

Both live games ship a single Unity codebase built for iOS and Android. The Unity client is a fairly thin presentation layer: it renders the board, handles input and local animation, and caches recent state so a cold start feels instant. Authoritative game logic — economy, matchmaking, progression, anti-cheat validation — lives server-side. Clients talk to the backend over HTTPS/JSON and hold a short-lived session token issued at login.

  • Store builds are cut from Unity Cloud Build; release tagging is manual per title.
  • Attribution and install tracking go through Singular; there is no second attribution SDK in the client.
  • Telemetry is emitted from the client and does not hit the backend directly — see the analytics section below.

Backend services

Backend services are written in Elixir/Phoenix and run as containers on AWS ECS Fargate behind a single shared Application Load Balancer. Each service is its own task definition and target group, routed by host/path rule at the ALB. State is persisted in Aurora PostgreSQL (RDS, Multi-AZ in prod). We lean on Elixir's supervision trees and BEAM concurrency so a crashing session process never takes down the node. Details and the service catalog live on Backend Services — Elixir/Phoenix.

Social & multiplayer

The social and real-time multiplayer layer is Nakama, run as its own Fargate service against a dedicated Aurora database. Nakama owns friends, leaderboards, chat, and the authoritative match runtime for head-to-head modes in Combo Fighter and GoD. Our Phoenix services call Nakama over its internal API rather than reimplementing sessions or presence. Operational runbooks are on Nakama Server Setup & Operations.

Component summary

ComponentTechRuns onNotes
Game clientUnity (C#)iOS / AndroidThin client; one codebase per title
Game backendElixir / PhoenixECS Fargate + ALBAuthoritative economy & progression
Social / multiplayerNakamaECS FargateFriends, leaderboards, chat, matches
Primary datastoreAurora PostgreSQLRDS (Multi-AZ)Separate cluster per service group
Infra as codeAWS CDK v2CISingle account per environment

Telemetry & analytics

Gameplay and monetization events flow from the Unity client into Firebase, are streamed into AWS Kinesis, transformed by AWS Glue, and landed in S3 for the warehouse. The backend is deliberately out of this path so a telemetry spike never adds load to the game services. The full pipeline, schemas, and dashboards are documented on Analytics Integration — Unity → Snowflake.

Keep this page conceptual. Do not paste account IDs, ALB DNS names, connection strings, or bundle IDs here — those belong in the AWS Infrastructure Guide and the secrets manager, not the wiki.

Owner: Frederick Stone (Growth/UA). This page is the map of our Metabase dashboards. Analysts run everything against the Snowflake BI layer, which is fed from the S3 event lake \\u2014 for how telemetry gets from the Unity client into that warehouse, see Analytics Integration \\u2014 Unity \\u2192 Snowflake.

Metabase is the reporting front-end only \\u2014 it holds saved questions and dashboards, not the source of truth. Every card queries Snowflake marts. If a dashboard looks stale, check the warehouse load first (the COPY runs on a schedule), not Metabase.

Standard dashboards

These are the dashboards we keep pinned and review on a regular cadence. They cover the full loop from acquisition through retention and monetization. Names are illustrative \\u2014 the actual collection names in Metabase may differ slightly, but the purpose and audience below are what matters.

DashboardPurposeAudience
DAU & RetentionDaily active users, session length, and D1/D7/D30 retention curves by title and cohort.Whole studio; reviewed at Monday standup.
FTUE FunnelFirst-time-user-experience completion \\u2014 level start / complete / fail drop-off through the onboarding funnel.Product & game design.
UA / CPI / ROAS by ChannelUser acquisition performance \\u2014 spend, installs, blended and per-channel CPI, and D7/D30 ROAS, joined from Singular attribution.Growth/UA (Frederick); exec on investor prep.
Monetization \\u2014 IAP / ARPUIn-app-purchase revenue, ARPU / ARPPU, conversion, and Season Pass attach + completion.Product & finance.
Live-Event PerformanceParticipation, completion, and revenue lift per live event vs baseline days.Live-ops & product.

How to read them

  • Every card is date-partitioned; default range is the trailing 28 days. Widen the filter for launch-window cohort views.
  • UA numbers reconcile to Singular, not to store console \\u2014 attribution windows differ, so expect small deltas.
  • Retention is measured on activity, not installs; a reinstall inside the window counts as a returning user, not a new one.

Metric definitions live with the OKRs

This page tells you which dashboard to open. It does not define what a metric means. D1 retention, blended CPI, D30 ROAS, ARPU \\u2014 those definitions, and the targets we hold them to, are owned alongside the objectives in Product OKRs \\u2014 2025 H1. If a dashboard number and an OKR number disagree, the OKR definition wins and the Metabase card is the thing to fix.

Do not fork a dashboard to \\\"redefine\\\" a metric for one analysis. If you need a variant (e.g. per-channel D1 instead of blended), add a card to the existing collection so the definition stays traceable. Silent metric drift between a fork and the canonical card is how two people end up quoting different D1 numbers in the same meeting.

Titles currently instrumented into these dashboards: Zombie Match 3D (store name Puzzles vs Zombies), Domino Delights (codename GoD), and Combo Fighter. All three share one event pipeline, so the same dashboard filters to any title.

Welcome to Harmony Games, Inc. (harmonygames.co). This is the studio overview for new hires — who we are, what we're building, and how we work. Read it first, then jump to the space for your discipline.

Who we are

Harmony Games is a small, remote-first mobile-game studio, founded in March 2023 and incorporated the following month in Delaware. We build hybrid-casual puzzle games — titles with the instant approachability of a casual game and the retention hooks of a light RPG. The team is distributed across three continents and runs lean by design (around sixteen people at its peak), keeping everyone close to the product.

The founding thesis comes from a specific background: 10+ years in gaming marketing plus a psychology degree. That pairing is the whole company in one sentence — we sit on the seam between marketing and product, and build games where the acquisition funnel and the core loop are designed together rather than handed off.

Mission

“A game of dominoes is really just match-3 in disguise — the same metrics, the same funnel. The opportunity is to take that casual approachability and deepen it: collection mechanics and a light RPG economy that give a player a reason to come back on day 30. Bridge marketing and product, and you get a game that is both cheap to acquire for and worth staying in.”

What we're building

Our titles, in the order the studio's focus moved to each:

WhenTitleDetail
Mar–Apr 2023Founded & incorporatedHarmony Games, Inc. founded March 2023; Delaware incorporation April 2023.
2023–2024Domino DelightsFirst title (internal codename "Game of Dominoes" / GoD) — tile-match with collection meta; benchmarked against Domino Dreams.
Jan 2025Zombie Match 3DStudio focus shifts to the match-3D RPG (store name "Puzzles vs Zombies"), benchmarked against Match Factory.
2025Combo Fighter (prototype)A third concept taken to prototype to test whether the hybrid-casual formula generalises beyond tile-match.

How we measure success

We measure product ambition against a fundability bar — the retention, CPI, and ROAS a growth round is underwritten on. That scorecard lives in Product OKRs \\u2014 2025 H1. Attribution across every title is standardised on Singular.

Where we are today: we've hit our tactical targets (ship dates, CPI), but day-30 retention and payback haven't yet cleared the bar a growth round is priced on. After the October 2025 cost reductions we're running on a lean core team while we pursue a bridge or strategic outcome to fund the next iteration. The near-term focus is proving day-30 retention holds — in hybrid-casual, the marketing-and-product seam only pays off if players stay past day one.

\", \"body_format\": \"storage\", \"status\": \"current\", \"version\": 6, \"author_id\": \"user_EMPLOYEE_0038\", \"created_at\": \"2023-04-01T12:00:44Z\", \"updated_at\": \"2025-09-01T10:36:32Z\"}, {\"id\": \"page_support_playbook\", \"space_id\": \"space_OPS\", \"parent_id\": \"page_ops_home\", \"title\": \"Customer Support Playbook\", \"body\": \"

First-line playbook for the four player-facing issues that drive the bulk of our inbound. It lets anyone covering the queue triage, reply, and escalate consistently. Scope is the live titles: Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" in stores) and Combo Fighter. When a symptom matches a known incident, say so plainly and give a real ETA rather than a canned apology.

Always capture platform + store version + device model and, where the player can find it, their in-game user id (Settings → About → tap the build number). Most escalations stall because the ticket is missing one of these.

Triage table

Match the reported symptom to the row, apply the resolution, and only escalate if the resolution does not clear it.

SymptomLikely causeFirst-line resolutionEscalate to
Lives not regenerating / timer stuckJuly 2025 scheduler outage (event/lives loop stalled)Confirm the window; grant a lives top-up as goodwill; reassure that regeneration resumes once the scheduler is advancingBackend (Live-Ops scheduler)
Lost progression / account back at level 1June 2025 device-ID wipe (new device id, old save orphaned)Look up the old user id by email/receipt and re-link the current install (see below)Backend (account re-link)
Quests not appearing / empty slotsNov 2024 quest incident (population/reset regression)Force a session refresh; if slots stay empty, collect user id + timestamp and flagDesign + Backend (quests)
Frozen on splash at ~22%May 2025 font/asset download stallAsk them to switch networks (Wi-Fi ↔ cellular), clear app cache, and reinstall; confirm it reaches gameplayClient / QA

Account re-link (June 2025 wipe)

A device-ID change orphaned some saves, dropping players to a fresh level-1 account while their real progression still exists under the previous id. Do not tell them the data is gone.

  • Ask for the account email and, ideally, a store receipt or order id.
  • Look up the old user id in the support console by that email; confirm the level/coin balance matches their description.
  • File a re-link request to Backend with both ids so the current install points at the old save.

Never issue a compensating grant before a re-link \\u2014 you would be topping up the empty new account, not the recovered one, and the balances double up after the merge. Grants come after the save is restored.

Canned responses

Personalise the greeting, keep the facts. Do not promise fixes we have not shipped.

  • Lives stuck: \\\"We had a scheduler issue that paused life regeneration for some players; it's being addressed and your lives will resume filling automatically. I've added a top-up in the meantime.\\\"
  • Lost progress: \\\"Your progression isn't lost \\u2014 a device change created a new profile. Send me the email on the account and I'll re-link it to your original save.\\\"
  • Missing quests: \\\"Quests should repopulate after a fresh session. If they're still empty, reply with your user id and when you noticed and I'll escalate.\\\"
  • Stuck at 22%: \\\"That's a loading stall on our end. Please switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data, clear the app cache, and reinstall.\\\"

Known-issue notes arrive from QA before a build ships \\u2014 see the QA Regression Runbook \\u2014 and symptoms found during a submission are mirrored here via the Release Checklist & Store Submission.

\", \"body_format\": \"storage\", \"status\": \"current\", \"version\": 9, \"author_id\": \"user_EMPLOYEE_0012\", \"created_at\": \"2024-07-01T17:26:08Z\", \"updated_at\": \"2025-07-26T08:50:17Z\"}, {\"id\": \"page_domino_gdd\", \"space_id\": \"space_PROD\", \"parent_id\": \"page_prod_home\", \"title\": \"Domino Delights \\u2014 Game Design Document\", \"body\": \"

Domino Delights (internal codename \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\" / GoD) is Harmony Games' tile-connecting puzzle title with light-RPG progression. This document is the living design reference for the core loop, character system, and retention mini-games. Store title is Domino Delights; use Game of Dominoes or GoD internally.

Soft-launched under the Baklava release (~Aug 2024). ~4,000 levels are in production. This GDD supersedes the pre-soft-launch draft; see the version history for the edit trail.

Core Loop & Mechanics

Players connect and match adjacent dominoes on a board to clear level objectives. Each cleared cluster feeds a combo meter; sustained combos drive the light-RPG layer, where collected characters level up and unlock stronger board-clearing abilities. A single run alternates between board-clearing turns and character-ability triggers, keeping session length short but replayable across the ~4,000-level ladder.

Boosts

  • Magical Gust \\u2014 a wind boost that clears all face-up tiles on the board, resetting a stalled position.
  • Character abilities (below) act as targeted boosts that recharge through matching.

For coin, life, and booster balancing that these mechanics feed into, see Economy Design \\u2014 Coins, Lives & Boosters.

Characters

Five collectible characters, each with its own upgrade track. Leveling a character deepens its signature effect and reduces its recharge cost.

CharacterSignature abilityUpgrade track
SophieDrops massive tiles that clear a wide area on contactIncreases tile size and blast radius
NathanRemoves a set of random tiles from the boardIncreases tiles removed per trigger
JuliusChains matches across the board for a combo bonusExtends chain length and combo multiplier
WildcardAdapts to the current objective, filling in the scarcest tile typeImproves match accuracy and recharge speed
Fifth (TBD)Reserved slot for the next collection waveDesign pending post-soft-launch data

Character names and the fifth slot are provisional. Do not surface upgrade numbers in marketing until the economy pass locks recharge costs.

Retention Mini-Games

Between level runs, players can enter reward mini-games that keep engagement high on off-days:

  • Tile Dozer \\u2014 a coin-pusher where dropped tiles shove a stacked tray toward the edge for coin and booster payouts.
  • Plinko \\u2014 a drop-and-bounce board awarding tiered rewards by landing slot.
  • Conveyor Belt \\u2014 a timed grab mini-game where players pull prizes off a moving belt.

Reward scaling for Tile Dozer and the other mini-games is tuned to daily-return targets and shares the coin sink with the core economy.

Competitive Context

Positioning benchmarks against the tile-matching leader are tracked in Competitive Analysis \\u2014 Match Factory.

Manual QA regression pass run against every release candidate before we submit a build for review. Owned by QA (Vincent); anyone cutting a build can run it, but a green matrix here is a gate on the Release Checklist & Store Submission. Scope covers Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (store name \\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\") and Combo Fighter. Keep it to ~45 minutes per title; if something fails, file the bug and block the release, don't hand-wave it.

Test the UPDATE path, not just a fresh install. The June 2025 ZM3D progression wipe only reproduced when updating from a previously-shipped version — a clean install looked perfectly healthy. Every candidate must be installed over the last two shipped versions and checked for save/progression loss before we ship. If we only test fresh installs we will miss this entire class of bug again.

Recurring bug classes to always check

These four have all bitten us in production. Treat them as non-negotiable checks on every pass, on real devices, not just the emulator.

  • Font / asset download stall on splash. In May 2025 ZM3D froze at roughly 22% on the splash screen while pulling remote fonts and assets. Watch the loading bar all the way to gameplay; test on a throttled/slow connection and with the app cache cleared.
  • Lives & scheduler regeneration. Confirm lives tick back up on the timer, refill correctly after device clock changes, and that offline time is credited without over-granting.
  • Quest population & reset. New quests populate on a fresh session, complete correctly, and roll over at the daily/weekly reset without duplicating or leaving empty slots.
  • Save / progression integrity. Level, coins and unlocks survive an update, a force-quit and a re-launch. This is the one the June 2025 wipe belongs to.

Regression matrix

Run each row on at least one iOS and one Android device. Both update rows are mandatory — N-1 and N-2 are the last two shipped store versions.

AreaFresh installUpdate from N-1Update from N-2Notes
Splash / asset loadPassPassPassWatch for the ~22% stall (May 2025 ZM3D)
Save / progressionPassPassPassJune 2025 wipe reproduced on update only
Lives & schedulerPassPassPassTest with device clock changes
Quests populate / resetPassPassPassCheck daily + weekly rollover
Purchase / restorePassPassPassSandbox account; confirm entitlements restore

If a check fails

  • File the bug with device, OS version, source build and repro steps, and link it here.
  • A failure in any UPDATE column blocks the release — fresh-install-only regressions do not pass the gate.
  • Player-facing symptoms (lost progress, stuck splash, missing lives) should be mirrored to the Customer Support Playbook so support has a known-issue note before it hits the store.

Once the matrix is green, tick the QA sign-off on the Release Checklist & Store Submission before submitting to the stores.

Per-title regression matrix

Each release candidate is walked through the full matrix below on at least one iOS and one Android device. A cell fails the gate if the observed behaviour deviates from the expected column; file the bug, mark the matrix red, and block the submission.

\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n
AreaCheckExpectedDominoZM3DCombo

EconomyEarn + spend coins, buy a boosterBalances reconcile; booster consumed onceYesYesn/a

\\n

Known-issue regression cases

These are the incidents that have bitten us in production; every one now has a permanent regression case so it cannot silently return. Reproduce the trigger, confirm the fix holds.

\\n

Font-download stall. On a fresh device the dynamic font pack could fail to download, freezing the UI at ~22% of the tutorial. Regression: install on a wiped device with a throttled connection; confirm a fallback font renders and load continues.

Device lab

The minimum matrix is one recent + one old device per platform. We keep a small physical lab plus a cloud device farm for the long tail.

Sign-off

QA posts the completed matrix in #ops and links it from the release ticket. A build without a green matrix does not get submitted \\u2014 no exceptions during the weekday release window, and never on a Friday.

This page describes the Elixir/Phoenix backend services that sit behind the Harmony Games clients \\u2014 Domino Delights (\\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"/GoD internally), Zombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" in-store), and Combo Fighter. The services own authoritative game state, player profiles, quests, and live-ops delivery. For the wider system picture and how these tie into Unity and Nakama, see Architecture Overview; realtime multiplayer and matchmaking are documented separately in Nakama Server Setup & Operations.

Ownership is deliberately thin \\u2014 a ~16-person studio can't staff a service mesh. One Elixir umbrella app, one Aurora cluster, a handful of Fargate tasks. Prefer boring and observable over clever.

Runtime & deployment

All services run as a single Elixir umbrella project, released with mix release and packaged into one container image. We run separate ECS Fargate services off that image (state, profile, quests, live-ops) so we can scale and roll them independently without maintaining separate codebases. Persistence is a shared Aurora PostgreSQL cluster with a schema per bounded context; the reader endpoint is used for analytics-adjacent queries so we don't contend with write traffic.

  • Compute: ECS Fargate, one task definition per service, behind an internal ALB.
  • Data: Aurora PostgreSQL (Multi-AZ), Ecto for access, migrations gated in CI.
  • Infra as code: everything provisioned via AWS CDK \\u2014 VPC, clusters, task definitions, and Aurora are all defined in the CDK app so environments (staging/prod) stay in lockstep.

Auth

There is no third-party auth broker. A small custom identity service issues short-lived JWTs on login; every other service validates the JWT signature locally (no per-request network hop) and trusts the sub claim as the player ID. Device-bound refresh tokens are stored in the identity service's own schema. Live-ops and quest mutations additionally require an internal service token \\u2014 never a player JWT.

Services

ServiceResponsibilityDatastore
identityLogin, JWT issuance/rotation, device bindingAurora (schema: identity)
game_stateAuthoritative match/board state, progression, save reconciliationAurora (schema: state)
profilePlayer profile, inventory, wallet (coins/lives)Aurora (schema: profile)
questsQuest definitions, assignment, and completion trackingAurora (schema: quests)
live_opsEvent scheduling, feature-flag delivery, seasonal contentAurora (schema: liveops)

Endpoints & releasing

Phoenix serves a thin JSON API \\u2014 no HTML, no channels here (realtime lives in Nakama). Routes are versioned under /api/v1 and health-checked at /healthz for the ALB. A representative controller and the release command:

elixir id}) do\\n case Profile.get_player(id) do\\n {:ok, player} -> json(conn, %{id: player.id, coins: player.coins, lives: player.lives})\\n {:error, :not_found} -> conn |> put_status(:not_found) |> json(%{error: \\\"not_found\\\"})\\n end\\n end\\nend\\n\\n# Build + run the release (baked into the Fargate image)\\n# MIX_ENV=prod mix release harmony_backend\\n# _build/prod/rel/harmony_backend/bin/harmony_backend start]]>

Migrations do not run on boot. Run bin/harmony_backend eval \\\"HarmonyBackend.Release.migrate()\\\" as a one-off Fargate task before rolling the services, so a bad migration can't take down every task at once.

Owner: Douglas. Ping in #eng-backend before schema changes to the shared Aurora cluster \\u2014 profile and game_state both read the wallet columns.

Combo Fighter is a merge / auto-battler prototype: the player drags Tetris-shaped pieces onto a board, merges matching pieces to upgrade them, connects them into combos, and then watches an auto-battle phase resolve the round. It was the last new concept Harmony Games took to a testable build \\u2014 a skeleton crew put a playable MVP together in roughly four to five weeks (late 2025 into January 2026). Of the three prototypes we shipped to store test tracks it posted the strongest early engagement, but it remains parked: we haven't put UA spend behind it yet to see whether that engagement holds at scale.

Core Mechanics

A round has two distinct phases. The build phase is board manipulation; the battle phase is hands-off resolution.

Build phase

  • Drag & place. The tray offers Tetris-shaped pieces (I, L, S, T, square). The player drags a piece onto the board; it snaps to the grid.
  • Merge to upgrade. Two same-tier pieces of the same type that touch merge into the next tier \\u2014 the familiar merge-2 loop, but on shaped pieces rather than single cells.
  • Connect for combos. Pieces wired into a contiguous chain form a combo; longer chains grant a battle-phase multiplier, so board layout drives power.

Battle phase

  • The assembled board becomes the player's squad and auto-battles the level's wave. No input during battle \\u2014 the round is won or lost on how the board was built.
  • Rewards are gold only. Gold funds re-rolls and starting-piece upgrades. No gems, no energy, no second currency in the MVP.

Ads: None in MVP. There is no ad SDK, no interstitials, and no rewarded placements in the prototype. Monetization was deliberately deferred until the core loop proved it retained \\u2014 the test builds measured engagement and retention only.

Art direction

Simple Chibi-style 3D characters on a clean board. The look was chosen to be cheap to produce at prototype scale while still reading as a finished game in a store screenshot.

Scope \\u2014 MVP

The build track was a 35-level MVP carved out of a 163-level full design. The MVP existed to answer one question \\u2014 does the merge-plus-auto-battle loop hold a player past the first session \\u2014 before committing to the remaining content and the deeper progression curve.

  • Shipped in MVP: 35 levels, drag/merge/connect build loop, auto-battle resolution, gold economy, Chibi 3D art.
  • Designed but not built: levels 36\\u2013163, meta-progression between runs, monetization surface, live-ops events.

Builds & Early Retention

Three test builds went out over roughly two weeks in January and early February 2026. D1 retention climbed with each build even as install volume swung with test-track promotion.

BuildRelease dateInstallsD1 retention
1.0.62Jan 21, 202612725%
1.0.72Jan 25, 202624431%
1.0.88Feb 4, 20263043%

Session length was the standout signal: Combo Fighter averaged roughly 60 minutes of play on the day of install (D0) \\u2014 the best of the three games we prototyped. By 1.0.88 the loop was tightening and D1 had reached 43% on a small install base, but we have not yet validated that at scale on a larger install base.

Related Pages

Prototype targets and the retention bar this work was measured against live in the H1 product objectives: Product OKRs \\u2014 2025 H1.

This page documents how gameplay telemetry flows from the Unity client into our analytics warehouse. It is the reference for anyone instrumenting a new event or writing a Snowflake query for a dashboard. For where this sits in the broader system, see Architecture Overview.

Scope: hybrid-casual titles across the studio \\u2014 Domino Delights (codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" on store), and Combo Fighter. All three share one instrumentation library and one pipeline.

Pipeline overview

The Unity client emits events through the Firebase Analytics SDK. From there a game-analytics pipeline streams events into AWS, transforms them, and lands them in object storage, from which the warehouse loads. The stages:

  • Unity client \\u2192 Firebase \\u2014 the client batches events and hands them to the Firebase Analytics SDK on-device.
  • Firebase \\u2192 Kinesis \\u2014 events are forwarded into an AWS Kinesis stream for ingestion.
  • Kinesis \\u2192 Glue \\u2014 an AWS Glue job validates and transforms records (flattens the event envelope, casts types, partitions by date).
  • Glue \\u2192 S3 \\u2014 both a raw/ and a processed/ prefix are written to S3.
  • S3 \\u2192 Snowflake \\u2014 the BI/warehouse layer loads from the S3 processed/ prefix. Analysts query Snowflake for dashboards and ad-hoc analysis.

Install attribution is handled separately by Singular (our MMP); attribution results are joined into Snowflake for UA reporting rather than flowing through the client event stream.

Event categories

Every event carries a common envelope (app version, platform, device class, session id, server timestamp). At a high level events fall into five categories:

CategoryFires onUsed for
SessionApp open / close, foreground / backgroundDAU, session length, retention curves
ProgressionLevel start / complete / failDifficulty tuning, funnel drop-off
Resource / economyCurrency and life grant / spendSink-source balance, economy health
Ad impressionRewarded / interstitial shown & completedAd revenue, fill rate, eCPM
Client errorHandled exceptions, load stallsCrash triage, release health

Load macro (Glue \\u2192 S3 \\u2192 Snowflake)

The warehouse pulls the Glue output from S3 with a scheduled COPY. Sketch of the load:

sql

The COPY is append-only and idempotent per partition \\u2014 never TRUNCATE the landing table to \\\"reload\\\", or you drop history the marts depend on. Backfills replay a specific dt= partition only.

Adding or changing an event

  • Register the event name and payload in the shared instrumentation library before shipping \\u2014 do not free-type event names in game code.
  • New fields must be nullable; the Glue transform tolerates extra keys but will not backfill missing ones.
  • Flag any type change (int \\u2192 string, etc.) to eng before release \\u2014 it breaks the Snowflake COPY column mapping.

This page describes the runtime architecture behind Harmony Games' live mobile titles — Domino Delights (internal codename Game of Dominoes / GoD) and Zombie Match 3D (store name Puzzles vs Zombies) — plus the shared platform that Combo Fighter and future titles ride on. It is the canonical starting point for new engineers; deep-dives live on the linked pages.

All of this runs in a single AWS account per environment (staging and prod). Infra is defined in AWS CDK (v2, TypeScript) — there is no click-ops. If it's not in the CDK app, it doesn't exist. See the AWS Infrastructure Guide for the account layout and deploy flow.

Client tier

Both live games ship a single Unity codebase built for iOS and Android. The Unity client is a fairly thin presentation layer: it renders the board, handles input and local animation, and caches recent state so a cold start feels instant. Authoritative game logic — economy, matchmaking, progression, anti-cheat validation — lives server-side. Clients talk to the backend over HTTPS/JSON and hold a short-lived session token issued at login.

  • Store builds are cut from Unity Cloud Build; release tagging is manual per title.
  • Attribution and install tracking go through Singular; there is no second attribution SDK in the client.
  • Telemetry is emitted from the client and does not hit the backend directly — see the analytics section below.

Backend services

Backend services are written in Elixir/Phoenix and run as containers on AWS ECS Fargate behind a single shared Application Load Balancer. Each service is its own task definition and target group, routed by host/path rule at the ALB. State is persisted in Aurora PostgreSQL (RDS, Multi-AZ in prod). We lean on Elixir's supervision trees and BEAM concurrency so a crashing session process never takes down the node. Details and the service catalog live on Backend Services — Elixir/Phoenix.

Social & multiplayer

The social and real-time multiplayer layer is Nakama, run as its own Fargate service against a dedicated Aurora database. Nakama owns friends, leaderboards, chat, and the authoritative match runtime for head-to-head modes in Combo Fighter and GoD. Our Phoenix services call Nakama over its internal API rather than reimplementing sessions or presence. Operational runbooks are on Nakama Server Setup & Operations.

Component summary

ComponentTechRuns onNotes
Game clientUnity (C#)iOS / AndroidThin client; one codebase per title
Game backendElixir / PhoenixECS Fargate + ALBAuthoritative economy & progression
Social / multiplayerNakamaECS FargateFriends, leaderboards, chat, matches
Primary datastoreAurora PostgreSQLRDS (Multi-AZ)Separate cluster per service group
Infra as codeAWS CDK v2CISingle account per environment

Telemetry & analytics

Gameplay and monetization events flow from the Unity client into Firebase, are streamed into AWS Kinesis, transformed by AWS Glue, and landed in S3 for the warehouse. The backend is deliberately out of this path so a telemetry spike never adds load to the game services. The full pipeline, schemas, and dashboards are documented on Analytics Integration — Unity → Snowflake.

Keep this page conceptual. Do not paste account IDs, ALB DNS names, connection strings, or bundle IDs here — those belong in the AWS Infrastructure Guide and the secrets manager, not the wiki.

Welcome to Harmony Games, Inc. (harmonygames.co). This is the studio overview for new hires — who we are, what we're building, and how we work. Read it first, then jump to the space for your discipline.

Who we are

Harmony Games is a small, remote-first mobile-game studio, founded in March 2023 and incorporated the following month in Delaware. We build hybrid-casual puzzle games — titles with the instant approachability of a casual game and the retention hooks of a light RPG. The team is distributed across three continents and runs lean by design (around sixteen people at its peak), keeping everyone close to the product.

The founding thesis comes from a specific background: 10+ years in gaming marketing plus a psychology degree. That pairing is the whole company in one sentence — we sit on the seam between marketing and product, and build games where the acquisition funnel and the core loop are designed together rather than handed off.

Mission

“A game of dominoes is really just match-3 in disguise — the same metrics, the same funnel. The opportunity is to take that casual approachability and deepen it: collection mechanics and a light RPG economy that give a player a reason to come back on day 30. Bridge marketing and product, and you get a game that is both cheap to acquire for and worth staying in.”

What we're building

Our titles, in the order the studio's focus moved to each:

WhenTitleDetail
Mar–Apr 2023Founded & incorporatedHarmony Games, Inc. founded March 2023; Delaware incorporation April 2023.
2023–2024Domino DelightsFirst title (internal codename "Game of Dominoes" / GoD) — tile-match with collection meta; benchmarked against Domino Dreams.
Jan 2025Zombie Match 3DStudio focus shifts to the match-3D RPG (store name "Puzzles vs Zombies"), benchmarked against Match Factory.
2025Combo Fighter (prototype)A third concept taken to prototype to test whether the hybrid-casual formula generalises beyond tile-match.

How we measure success

We measure product ambition against a fundability bar — the retention, CPI, and ROAS a growth round is underwritten on. That scorecard lives in Product OKRs \\u2014 2025 H1. Attribution across every title is standardised on Singular.

Where we are today: we've hit our tactical targets (ship dates, CPI), but day-30 retention and payback haven't yet cleared the bar a growth round is priced on. After the October 2025 cost reductions we're running on a lean core team while we pursue a bridge or strategic outcome to fund the next iteration. The near-term focus is proving day-30 retention holds — in hybrid-casual, the marketing-and-product seam only pays off if players stay past day one.

First-line playbook for the four player-facing issues that drive the bulk of our inbound. It lets anyone covering the queue triage, reply, and escalate consistently. Scope is the live titles: Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" in stores) and Combo Fighter. When a symptom matches a known incident, say so plainly and give a real ETA rather than a canned apology.

Always capture platform + store version + device model and, where the player can find it, their in-game user id (Settings → About → tap the build number). Most escalations stall because the ticket is missing one of these.

Triage table

Match the reported symptom to the row, apply the resolution, and only escalate if the resolution does not clear it.

SymptomLikely causeFirst-line resolutionEscalate to
Lives not regenerating / timer stuckJuly 2025 scheduler outage (event/lives loop stalled)Confirm the window; grant a lives top-up as goodwill; reassure that regeneration resumes once the scheduler is advancingBackend (Live-Ops scheduler)
Lost progression / account back at level 1June 2025 device-ID wipe (new device id, old save orphaned)Look up the old user id by email/receipt and re-link the current install (see below)Backend (account re-link)
Quests not appearing / empty slotsNov 2024 quest incident (population/reset regression)Force a session refresh; if slots stay empty, collect user id + timestamp and flagDesign + Backend (quests)
Frozen on splash at ~22%May 2025 font/asset download stallAsk them to switch networks (Wi-Fi ↔ cellular), clear app cache, and reinstall; confirm it reaches gameplayClient / QA

Account re-link (June 2025 wipe)

A device-ID change orphaned some saves, dropping players to a fresh level-1 account while their real progression still exists under the previous id. Do not tell them the data is gone.

  • Ask for the account email and, ideally, a store receipt or order id.
  • Look up the old user id in the support console by that email; confirm the level/coin balance matches their description.
  • File a re-link request to Backend with both ids so the current install points at the old save.

Never issue a compensating grant before a re-link \\u2014 you would be topping up the empty new account, not the recovered one, and the balances double up after the merge. Grants come after the save is restored.

Canned responses

Personalise the greeting, keep the facts. Do not promise fixes we have not shipped.

  • Lives stuck: \\\"We had a scheduler issue that paused life regeneration for some players; it's being addressed and your lives will resume filling automatically. I've added a top-up in the meantime.\\\"
  • Lost progress: \\\"Your progression isn't lost \\u2014 a device change created a new profile. Send me the email on the account and I'll re-link it to your original save.\\\"
  • Missing quests: \\\"Quests should repopulate after a fresh session. If they're still empty, reply with your user id and when you noticed and I'll escalate.\\\"
  • Stuck at 22%: \\\"That's a loading stall on our end. Please switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data, clear the app cache, and reinstall.\\\"

Known-issue notes arrive from QA before a build ships \\u2014 see the QA Regression Runbook \\u2014 and symptoms found during a submission are mirrored here via the Release Checklist & Store Submission.

\", \"body_format\": \"storage\", \"status\": \"current\", \"version\": 9, \"author_id\": \"user_EMPLOYEE_0012\", \"created_at\": \"2024-07-01T17:26:08Z\", \"updated_at\": \"2025-07-26T08:50:17Z\"}, {\"id\": \"page_domino_gdd\", \"space_id\": \"space_PROD\", \"parent_id\": \"page_prod_home\", \"title\": \"Domino Delights \\u2014 Game Design Document\", \"body\": \"

Domino Delights (internal codename \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\" / GoD) is Harmony Games' tile-connecting puzzle title with light-RPG progression. This document is the living design reference for the core loop, character system, and retention mini-games. Store title is Domino Delights; use Game of Dominoes or GoD internally.

Soft-launched under the Baklava release (~Aug 2024). ~4,000 levels are in production. This GDD supersedes the pre-soft-launch draft; see the version history for the edit trail.

Core Loop & Mechanics

Players connect and match adjacent dominoes on a board to clear level objectives. Each cleared cluster feeds a combo meter; sustained combos drive the light-RPG layer, where collected characters level up and unlock stronger board-clearing abilities. A single run alternates between board-clearing turns and character-ability triggers, keeping session length short but replayable across the ~4,000-level ladder.

Boosts

  • Magical Gust \\u2014 a wind boost that clears all face-up tiles on the board, resetting a stalled position.
  • Character abilities (below) act as targeted boosts that recharge through matching.

For coin, life, and booster balancing that these mechanics feed into, see Economy Design \\u2014 Coins, Lives & Boosters.

Characters

Five collectible characters, each with its own upgrade track. Leveling a character deepens its signature effect and reduces its recharge cost.

CharacterSignature abilityUpgrade track
SophieDrops massive tiles that clear a wide area on contactIncreases tile size and blast radius
NathanRemoves a set of random tiles from the boardIncreases tiles removed per trigger
JuliusChains matches across the board for a combo bonusExtends chain length and combo multiplier
WildcardAdapts to the current objective, filling in the scarcest tile typeImproves match accuracy and recharge speed
Fifth (TBD)Reserved slot for the next collection waveDesign pending post-soft-launch data

Character names and the fifth slot are provisional. Do not surface upgrade numbers in marketing until the economy pass locks recharge costs.

Retention Mini-Games

Between level runs, players can enter reward mini-games that keep engagement high on off-days:

  • Tile Dozer \\u2014 a coin-pusher where dropped tiles shove a stacked tray toward the edge for coin and booster payouts.
  • Plinko \\u2014 a drop-and-bounce board awarding tiered rewards by landing slot.
  • Conveyor Belt \\u2014 a timed grab mini-game where players pull prizes off a moving belt.

Reward scaling for Tile Dozer and the other mini-games is tuned to daily-return targets and shares the coin sink with the core economy.

Competitive Context

Positioning benchmarks against the tile-matching leader are tracked in Competitive Analysis \\u2014 Match Factory.

Owned by QA (Vincent); anyone cutting a build can run it, but a green matrix here is a gate on the Release Checklist & Store Submission. Scope covers Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (store name \\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\") and Combo Fighter. These four have all bitten us in production. Treat them as non-negotiable checks on every pass, on real devices, not just the emulator.

Each release candidate is walked through the full matrix below on at least one iOS and one Android device. A cell fails the gate if the observed behaviour deviates from the expected column; file the bug, mark the matrix red, and block the submission.

These are the incidents that have bitten us in production; every one now has a permanent regression case so it cannot silently return. Reproduce the trigger, confirm the fix holds.

\\n
